run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation application (namespace hotel-reservation) is a brand-new instance created at 18:11:32-18:11:34Z, and from the moment traffic started its search path fails: frontend HTTP GET /hotels returns 500 because search.Search/Nearby errors, and search's own logs attribute the failures to dependency=rate with grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded (plus some ResourceExhausted). The deepest failure the evidence shows is inside the rate service: its admission queue is saturated (rate_queue_depth 255 against rate_queue_capacity 256, with 809 requests rejected and 916 expired), and a sampled rate server span shows a request waiting about 12.7 s before it even calls memcached, far beyond the 750 ms RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS the search client allows. Admitted rate requests are themselves fast (memcached children 0.5-0.8 ms; 275 of 277 GetRates spans <=1 ms) and neither the rate nor the search container is CPU-throttled, so the backing stores and pod CPU are not the bottleneck; the queue is shaped by the rate Deployment's admission settings (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256) together with search's retry budget (RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, 750 ms timeout). Because change history is not integrated, no baseline exists for this instance (application metric samples start 18:11:48Z), and the load generator is not observable, I cannot verify which setting was injected or whether offered load alone exceeds intended capacity; the conclusion is therefore partial and the rate-vs-retry-vs-load alternatives are kept as separate hypotheses.

claims.text: All 19 pods in namespace hotel-reservation are Running and ready, and every one of them was created between 2026-11-21T18:11:32Z and 18:11:34Z; rate-c4d7bcb48-hdhs6 and search-7769dfc66b-bmg9r are owned by ReplicaSets rate-c4d7bcb48 and search-7769dfc66b, and Deployments rate and search are at generation 1 with image digest sha256:1c685e1c..., so the whole application instance is only about two minutes old at the end of the window.

Pod search-7769dfc66b-bmg9r has restartCount 1 with last termination reason Error and exit code 1; its previous container log ends at 18:11:35Z with 'FTL cmd/search/main.go:75 > failed register: Put "http://consul:8500/v1/agent/service/register": dial tcp 10.96.78.107:8500: connect: connection refused', and the replacement container started at 18:11:36Z and logged 'Successfully registered in consul' at 18:11:37Z.

Deployment rate in namespace hotel-reservation sets container env RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256; Deployment search sets RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=50, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0 and RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2.

The rate service's own metrics report rate_backend_qps_limit=20 and rate_queue_capacity=256 on instance rate.hotel-reservation:9091, matching the Deployment env values, so both settings are in effect at runtime.

Between the samples at 18:12:58Z and 18:13:18Z the rate service's admission queue went from rate_queue_depth 0 to 255 against rate_queue_capacity 256, while rate_requests_received_total rose 223->2335, rate_requests_completed_total 223->1271, rate_requests_rejected_total 0->809 and rate_requests_expired_total 0->916.

Rate requests that are admitted are fast: of 277 traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket counts for service_name=rate span_name=/rate.Rate/GetRates, 275 are <=1 ms and 277 are <=100 ms, and in sampled traces the memcached_get_multi_rate child spans of rate measure 514-768 microseconds.

In sampled traces at 18:13:32-18:13:34Z the rate server span /rate.Rate/GetRates lasted 12.75-12.80 s while its child memcached_get_multi_rate span started about 12.7 s after the server span started, i.e. the request waited roughly 12.7 s inside the rate service before any backend work began.

Search's client spans /rate.Rate/GetRates end in error at 750.08-751.03 ms (the 750 ms client timeout), the parent search.Search/Nearby server spans last about 2.39 s (three sequential timed-out attempts), and pod search-7769dfc66b-bmg9r logs repeated 'downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded' lines, dozens per second at 18:13:20-18:13:32Z, plus grpc_code=ResourceExhausted.

Search's own rate-RPC counters record search_rate_attempts_total=1608, search_rate_successes_total=355, search_rate_failures_total=407 and search_rate_timeouts_total=550 (with search_requests_total=779), so most rate attempts made by search fail or time out.

Frontend spans show the user-visible symptom: HTTP GET /hotels server spans with error=true and http.status_code=500 lasting about 2.39-2.40 s, each with an error child span /search.Search/Nearby of about 2.39 s, in all three sampled frontend traces at 18:13:32-18:13:34Z.

The rate and search containers are not CPU-throttled: container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total is 0 for container hotel-reserv-rate in pod rate-c4d7bcb48-hdhs6 and for container hotel-reserv-search in pod search-7769dfc66b-bmg9r.

Rate's span metrics show 277 /rate.Rate/GetRates server spans and 5 mongo_rate spans, all labeled status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET (the rate side itself records no error status), whereas the failing client spans of /rate.Rate/GetRates are recorded under service_name=search with error=true.

Rate's backing stores are not the slow part: memcached_get_multi_rate spans complete in 514-768 microseconds and admitted GetRates requests finish in <=1 ms, while the multi-second delay occurs before the memcached call is made.
The geo dependency is not the failing downstream: /geo.Geo/Nearby spans measured 32-144 microseconds with no error tags in the same failing traces that show /rate.Rate/GetRates errors.

Rejected: the search pod's single restart caused the outage. That restart happened at 18:11:35Z because consul was not yet accepting registrations (connection refused on srv-geo/srv-rate lookups), before the pod registered successfully at 18:11:37Z and before traffic; the current container's error lines are all dependency=rate timeouts.

Rejected: CPU throttling or resource starvation of the rate or search containers produced the timeouts, since container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total is 0 for both containers and no pod is in a waiting or terminated state.

Primary hypothesis: the rate Deployment's admission-control settings (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 with RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256) cap admitted /rate.Rate/GetRates throughput below the offered load, so its queue saturates at 255/256, requests wait about 12.7 s and are expired or rejected (809 rejected, 916 expired), which exceeds search's 750 ms RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS and produces the DeadlineExceeded/ResourceExhausted errors, the search.Search/Nearby errors and the frontend /hotels 500s.

Alternative/contributing hypothesis: the search Deployment's retry policy (RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 with 50 ms initial backoff against a 750 ms per-attempt timeout) triples the offered rate-call load and keeps the rate queue full once the first timeouts occur, so search's settings could be the injected fault rather than the rate service's QPS limit.

Third hypothesis: the offered load itself (rate_requests_received_total rose 223->2335 between 18:12:58Z and 18:13:18Z) exceeded the intended capacity of a single 20 QPS rate service, i.e. the traffic source rather than a rate-code defect; no load generator is visible in namespace hotel-reservation, so this cannot be separated from the admission-limit hypothesis with the available evidence.

Compare RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 / RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 on Deployment rate and RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 / RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 on Deployment search against the reference configuration or source history to identify which value was injected, then restore the intended rate capacity (or scale rate replicas) and re-tune the search retry budget so retries do not keep the rate queue saturated.

gaps: Change history is not integrated (change_history unavailable), so I cannot verify when RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 or search's RATE_RPC_* values were set; both Deployments are at generation 1 and all pods were created at 18:11:32-18:11:34Z, so there is no pre-incident baseline for this application instance.

Metric samples for the hotel-reservation application only begin at 18:11:48Z (earliest source_start_at seen), so no 'before' reading exists to prove the rate limiter or the request load changed during the window.

The traffic source is not identified: no load-generator pod exists in namespace hotel-reservation and its offered QPS could not be measured, so the hypothesis that offered load exceeds intended rate capacity remains unverified.

The rate service's container logs contain only startup lines (18:11:34-18:11:40Z); there is no log evidence of the rejections or expiries themselves, and ResourceExhausted is attested only by search's log lines.

Queries for error-tagged traces of service profile and service reservation returned nothing (status no_data: fc6f35a6-1f75-4d93-9877-4ecaaf24c22a-t0, fc6f35a6-1f75-4d93-9877-4ecaaf24c22a-t1), and the frontend pod log query returned no lines (10913476-3271-4040-b573-d4f995967d7a-t0, no_data); these empty results do not prove those services or that pod were error-free, so profile, reservation, user, recommendation and geo health is unchecked beyond the geo spans seen inside search traces.

Prometheus returned no series for the rpc_* metric family (b310a612-c740-4e07-bffc-8ec928ecf326-t0 and -t1, no_data) and no metadata for search_rate_attempts_total (b8cae0a7-e736-4a5b-b1e5-a84fd7de4642-t0, no_data), and the search_rate_* series only appeared at two samples (18:12:33Z and 18:13:33Z), so gRPC status-code label coverage and finer resolution of those counters remain unknown.
Whether the rate service is meant to serve about 20 QPS, i.e. whether 20 is the injected value or the intended baseline, could not be verified.
next_steps: Retrieve the pre-change configuration or commit for Deployments rate and search (for example from manifest or repository history) to see which RATE_* values were injected and when.
Measure the load generator's offered request rate against the rate service's admitted throughput to confirm whether the 20 QPS limit or the search retry amplification is the primary constraint.

If the rate limit is confirmed as the fault, raise RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT / RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY to the intended values or scale the rate Deployment, and review search's RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS and RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS so retries do not amplify load.
